subject: Notice: Targeted EU & APAC region interruption — traffic bridge options
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acmemedia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: Targeted EU & APAC region interruption — traffic bridge options

Sarah —

Quick heads-up: between ~08:45–10:00 UTC we observed a targeted degradation affecting our EU edge POPs and a subset of APAC peering links. The control plane remained available; however a proportion of customer traffic originating in EU and APAC saw increased tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors when pinned to region-specific endpoints.

What you might have seen: brief slow responses or failed requests for sessions that were routed to EU/APAC-only endpoints. Most traffic to global endpoints remained healthy.

Immediate recommendation (actionable):
- Short-term: pivot traffic away from the EU/APAC region-specific endpoints to our global US ingress while we stabilize routing. We can provide a temporary endpoint list for cutover (attached: temporary-endpoints.csv).
- If you have an edge-steering or external load balancer, add the provided US ingress hosts with a higher priority and a low TTL (30s) for now.
- If you prefer, Redwood can enable automated edge steering for your account and perform the switch; this typically completes within 2–6 minutes and does not require code changes.

I’ve included Marissa (CSM) and Vanessa (Ops) on this thread to coordinate the cutover window. Markus is looping in the postmortem and mitigation plan.

Attachments: incident-runbook-summary.pdf (summary of current incident), temporary-endpoints.csv (CSV with temporary US ingress hosts)

Expected impact of the short-term switch: minimal functional change; you may see slightly higher latency for EU-origin traffic routed via US, but it will avoid error spikes. We will follow up with a written postmortem and evidence package for your auditors.

Can you confirm if you prefer us to: (A) enable automated steering on your behalf now, or (B) provide the endpoint list and checklist so your infra team can cut over? If you choose (B), please propose a 15–30 minute window in the next 60 minutes.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0123 | tessa.morgan@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: Targeted EU & APAC region interruption — traffic bridge options

Tessa —

Quick technical notes for the team and for Sarah if they want to DIY the switchover:

1) Edge steering toggle (recommended if customer says go):
- We have an account-level flag we can flip to enable automated client-side steering to US-ingress endpoints. This updates DNS TTLs and pushes new host preferences to our edge routers.
- Rollback is immediate; we can revert the steering in < 2 minutes.

2) Manual LB / DNS checklist (if doing customer-side):
- Add entries from temporary-endpoints.csv to your upstream/pool with weight 100 and set EU endpoints to weight 0 or remove them.
- Set DNS TTL to 30s for the cutover and monitor 5xx rate on your monitoring.
- Healthcheck path: GET /_health?probe=1 (200 expected).

3) Nginx example upstream change:
- upstream inference_backends {
-    server us-ingress-1.redwood.net:443 max_fails=3 fail_timeout=30s;
-    server eu-ingress-2.redwood.net:443 backup;
- }
- Use graceful reload (nginx -s reload) to avoid connection drops.

4) If the customer uses a CDN in front, ask their CDN vendor to set origin failover to the provided US origins.

I attached a quick script (edge-failover-script.sh) that can be run from an ops workstation to perform the upstream swap and verify health checks.

Vanessa
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 10:03:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: Targeted EU & APAC region interruption — traffic bridge options

Sarah —

Thanks for the quick reply. Per Vanessa’s note we can do the automated steering on your behalf now; we’ll run the change and monitor for 30 minutes. Below is a brief checklist we’ll follow and report back on each step. If you’d rather your infra team run it, I’ve pasted the same checklist and the temporary endpoints in the shared Drive.

Redwood-run checklist (what we will do if you approve):
1) Notify your on-call (Procurement/Infra) that we’ll start at T+5 minutes.
2) Flip account-level edge-steering flag to prefer US ingress.
3) Verify healthchecks across 3 probes (us-ingress-1/2/3).
4) Confirm 5xx rate drops to baseline for your traffic.
5) Produce an evidence bundle (logs, histograms) and share link.

Estimated customer-visible window: the change takes ~2–6 minutes to propagate to most sessions. We will keep the TTL low and monitor closely.

We’ll also issue a goodwill credit for the impacted window and include the full evidence bundle and postmortem in ~24–36 hours.

Please reply with a single word YES to authorize Redwood to perform the steering now, or NO to decline.

—
Tessa

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 18:04:10 +0200
Subject: Postmortem summary and next steps — 2028-06-15 EU/APAC edge degradation

Hi all —

Short postmortem summary (root cause & current status):
- What happened: A misconfiguration in a third-party peering fabric caused intermittent blackholing of control traffic to a subset of our EU edge POPs; concurrent BGP path flaps between two APAC regions caused higher-than-usual failover churn. The combined effect increased connection setup failures and 502/503 errors for sessions bound to region-specific ingress pools.

- Timeline (UTC):
  * 08:42 — First alarms: elevated TCP reset and 502 rates from eu-ingress-2 cluster.
  * 08:50 — Ops engagement and verification; began mitigation planning.
  * 09:12 — Customer advisories sent.
  * 09:18 — Account-level steering enabled for impacted customers (per authorization).
  * 09:25 — Majority of affected requests shifted to US ingress; 5xx rates returned to baseline by 09:32.

- Impact: For affected customers we estimate ~8–12% of requests (predominantly new session establishment from EU/APAC origin) experienced errors during the peak window. Tail latency increased ~200–400ms for sessions redirected via US.

- Short-term mitigations already completed:
  1) Temporary account-level steering to US ingress for impacted customers.
  2) Increased BGP dampening for noisy neighbors where available.
  3) Edge POP healthcheck tuning to reduce false positives.

- Long-term actions (owners & ETA):
  1) Peering resilience program: add alternate peering paths and stricter validation for control-plane announcements (owner: Network, ETA: 2028-07-31).
  2) Automated cross-region failover playbook & test (owner: Ops/Platform, ETA: 2028-08-15).
  3) Improved external visibility pack for customers (dashboard slice, evidence export) (owner: DevEx, ETA: 2028-07-10).

We will produce a full evidence bundle (logs, DNS snapshots, histograms) and place it in the Drive folder linked above within 24 hours. I’ll also coordinate a short follow-up call with Acme if they want to review the details.

If anyone needs additional detail for compliance reporting (SOC2 artifacts, ingress logs sliced by account), flag here and we’ll prioritize.

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Network & Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
